clue.text: Kind of recorder two notes short

parts.note: D and E are two notes of the musical scale; the plural covers both letters
D and E are two notes of the musical scale; the plural covers both letters
scant means short, in short supply

explanation.surface: A recorder that is two notes short of a full range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two notes' supplies two separate letters, D and E, before SCANT for 'short'.
explanation.definitionFit: The descant is the highest-pitched member of the recorder family, the one most schoolchildren learn.

clue.text: Talk about being second in Olympic event

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the event's name

parts.note: the discus throw is an Olympic field event

explanation.surface: Discussing a silver medal won at the Games.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss something is to talk it over, to debate it.

clue.text: But it is not normally in the grammar-school syllabus

definitions.text: But it is not normally in the grammar-school syllabus

parts.words: But it is not normally in the grammar-school syllabus
parts.note: a grammar school teaches grammar, but not how to pronounce and deliver words well; that lesson in elocution is something else

explanation.walkthrough: A grammar school is a selective British secondary school; the clue plays on 'grammar' as if the school taught only correct language, which it would, but not elocution.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessons in elocution and voice production are a kind of tuition for the spoken word.

clue.text: Yodeller's range?

parts.note: range is read as a mountain range rather than a vocal range; yodelling is the traditional song of Swiss and Austrian mountain folk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' suggests the span of notes a singer can reach; here it is the mountain chain where yodelling comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alpine mountain chain of Switzerland and Austria is home to the yodelling tradition.

clue.text: Heavyweight certain to have head shaven.

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer who is sure to get his head shaved.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk's or priest's head.

clue.text: We must take it in within the time allowed

indicators.note: within says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A deadline: something we must absorb before time runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' points inside 'the tiME ALlowed'; 'take it in' means eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is something we take in by eating, at a sitting such as lunch.

clue.text: Like 15's crowd, thousand joining

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
adding means joining on

explanation.surface: A crowd swollen by a thousand more people joining it.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is HARDY: Thomas Hardy wrote the novel Far from the Madding Crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective in the title of Hardy's novel describes a frenzied, frantic crowd.

clue.text: The first man to be a mother

definitions.meaning: in Genesis, the first human created by God
a dam is a mother animal

explanation.definitionFit: Genesis names the first man; split into two words it gives a dam, the female parent of livestock.

clue.text: Feeler put out by some workers

definitions.text: Feeler put out by some workers

parts.words: Feeler put out by some workers
parts.note: the workers are ants, insects that put out sensory feelers from their heads

explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' suggests employees; worker ants are the insects meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's feeler is the sensory organ on its head.

clue.text: Wild animal rage, is it providing theme for Orwell?

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: A ferocious beast's fury becoming the subject of Orwell's Animal Farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges ANIMAL RAGE IS IT; 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal Farm satirises the ideal of equality for all, with some animals more equal than others.

clue.text: Mix night-drug, please

indicators.note: mix tells us to blend the following letters into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone asking a pharmacist to make up a sleeping potion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix' rearranges NIGHT DRUG PLEASE, and the whole clue is a request for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A potion taken at bedtime to bring on slumber is a drug for the night.

clue.text: Union leaders firm — that's great for Jock

parts.note: the leading letters of the word union
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A trade union's leaders praising a company.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scot; unco is a Scots word meaning very or remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means remarkable or extremely, an intensifier.

clue.text: Composition of Orsino's 5?

definitions.meaning: a piece of composed work for instruments or voices
5 is MEAL; Orsino opens Twelfth Night with 'If ... be the food of love'

explanation.walkthrough: Duke Orsino in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night calls it the food of love, and food is a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition is a piece of melody and harmony, and Orsino calls it the food of love.

clue.text: Design for a tailless aircraft

indicators.note: tailless means the word loses its last letter, its tail

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

explanation.surface: A blueprint for an aircraft with no tail fin.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a scheme or drawing showing how something will be made.

clue.text: Type of flower much plagued by laurel…

definitions.meaning: a plant able to survive frost and cold
Oliver of the comic duo Laurel and ___, forever exasperated by Stan Laurel

explanation.walkthrough: 'laurel' looks like a shrub harming the plant; it is Stan Laurel of the comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust flowers that survive winter are so called, and Oliver was the partner Stan Laurel kept landing in trouble.

clue.text: … South American flower of unusual petal design

indicators.note: unusual tells us the petal's letters take an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: A South American bloom with oddly shaped petals.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows, a river: the River Plate in Argentina and Uruguay.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Plate is the estuary between Argentina and Uruguay, a flowing body of water.

clue.text: What makes us feed until full? AI taste, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Wondering what makes us eat until stuffed: perhaps an artificial taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AITASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To glut someone is to fill them to the point of being unable to eat more.

clue.text: Pygmalion's animated cast

parts.note: in Greek myth Pygmalion carved a statue of a woman which came to life; cast means a sculpted figure, animated means brought to life

explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a theatre cast for Shaw's play Pygmalion; it is the sculptor's statue in Ovid's myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ovid the ivory statue made by the sculptor was brought to life by Aphrodite.

clue.text: Set great store by

parts.note: the idiom means valued highly, but read literally it is set aside a great store, or stockpile

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for valuing something is read literally: a great store was put by.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockpiling goods means laying them away in a large secret stock.

clue.text: Stirred to a rich stew

indicators.note: stirred as in a pot, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Stirring a rich stew in the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirred' rearranges TO A RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: A haricot is a French ragout of mutton with vegetables.

clue.text: Act like a postman submitted to railing-climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: railing is abuse; to be subjected to it is to be reviled

explanation.surface: A postman made to climb over railings to drop off the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railing' looks like a fence; it is scolding, as in 'rail against'.
explanation.definitionFit: Postmen hand over letters and parcels to the addressee.

clue.text: Can they not be bought as presents?

definitions.text: Can they not be bought as presents?

parts.words: Can they not be bought as presents?
parts.note: presents reads as gifts but means the present time: these contracts are bought now for goods delivered at a later date

explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' suggests gifts; it is the present tense, the opposite of contracts for things to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Commodity contracts traded for later delivery belong to time yet to come, not now.

clue.text: More monotonous fellow, second of the two

parts.note: the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: Picking the duller of two men.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull, unvarying voice is called less lively, lacking any rise and fall.

clue.text: 13? Ollie's partner swallows standard

indicators.note: swallows means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: Stan Laurel was Oliver Hardy's comedy partner
par is the standard, as in golf

explanation.surface: Stan Laurel gulping down a regulation amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is HARDY in the sense of tough and frugal; Spartans were famed for austere toughness.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardy person and an austere, tough one both endure hardship without comforts.

clue.text: Payment for use of house in Split…

explanation.surface: Paying for a house in the Croatian city of Split.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant pays a landlord for housing, and something torn apart has been rent.

clue.text: … novel house, but starting to let rain in

indicators.note: starting points to the first letter of the word but

parts.note: a roof that lets rain in leaks

explanation.surface: A house that is new but already letting rain in.
explanation.walkthrough: With the ellipsis the clue reads as Dickens's novel Bleak House.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective completes the title of the Dickens novel about Jarndyce and Jarndyce.

clue.text: Fun for students, a form of Hindu music

parts.note: rag week is a British university tradition of fundraising pranks and fun

explanation.surface: Students having a laugh, playing Indian music.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG is the British student charity week of stunts and pranks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Indian classical music the raga is a melodic framework for improvisation.

clue.text: Same sort of hill, but 19 down

indicators.note: sort means put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A similar hill, only with a flat top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges SAME; 19 down is FLAT, so a hill with a level top.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableland is a steep-sided hill with a level summit, common in the American Southwest.

clue.text: Lear's had a light-giving bill

parts.note: Edward Lear's nonsense poem tells of a creature with a luminous nose; bill means a nose or beak, not an account

explanation.walkthrough: Not King Lear but Edward Lear, whose poem 'The ___ with a Luminous Nose' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear's nonsense character has a glowing nose.

clue.text: Soon, civet strain will break down. Who cares?

indicators.note: break down means come apart, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A civet's soon going to collapse under the strain, and nobody cares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will break down' rearranges SOON CIVET STRAIN. 'Who cares?' looks dismissive; it asks literally who cares for nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who protects wildlife and habitats is one who cares for the environment.

clue.text: Royal salmon

definitions.meaning: Catherine, sixth wife of Henry VIII and so a queen
a young salmon before it goes to sea

explanation.definitionFit: Catherine was Henry VIII's last queen, and a young river fish before the smolt stage carries the same name.

clue.text: Course of treatment for most of colonel's men

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: a colonel commands a regiment of soldiers

explanation.surface: A medical course prescribed for the bulk of a colonel's troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed programme of diet, exercise or medicine.
